title: Acute Otitis Media Assessment
summary: A clinician-facing prompt for assessing suspected acute otitis media, distinguishing uncomplicated middle-ear infection from important alternatives and complications, and supporting proportionate treatment, referral and safety-netting.

sections.title: Assessment priorities
sections.intro: Confirm that symptoms and otoscopy are compatible with acute otitis media, assess pain and systemic illness, and actively exclude mastoid or intracranial complications.

items.title: Must confirm or exclude
mustConfirmOrExclude: Acute otitis media with compatible symptoms and middle-ear inflammation.
Mastoiditis or another spreading local complication.
Meningitis, intracranial infection or facial nerve involvement.
Otitis externa, referred otalgia or another alternative diagnosis.
Tympanic membrane perforation or otorrhoea.
Severe systemic illness, dehydration or inability to take oral treatment.
Age, comorbidity or immunosuppression that increases complication risk.
items.importantLimitation: Ear pain alone does not diagnose acute otitis media. Diagnosis should be based on the clinical picture together with otoscopic evidence of middle-ear inflammation.

sections.title: Focused history
sections.intro: Define the time course, severity and associated upper-respiratory symptoms, then identify features suggesting a complication or alternative cause.

items.title: Presenting illness
mustConfirmOrExclude: Onset, duration and progression of ear pain.
Unilateral or bilateral symptoms.
Fever, irritability or systemic upset.
Hearing change, blocked sensation or tinnitus.
Otorrhoea or sudden change in pain suggesting perforation.
Recent upper-respiratory infection.
Previous recurrent otitis media, perforation, grommets or ear surgery.

items.title: Features suggesting complication
mustConfirmOrExclude: Post-auricular pain, swelling or redness.
Pinna protrusion or increasing mastoid tenderness.
Severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting or altered mental state.
New facial weakness.
Persistent or rapidly worsening symptoms despite treatment.

items.title: Background risk
mustConfirmOrExclude: Very young age or significant comorbidity.
Immunosuppression or craniofacial abnormality.
Cochlear implant or other relevant ear device.
Known drug allergies and recent antimicrobial exposure.
Ability to maintain fluids, analgesia and follow-up.

sections.title: Red flags and complications
sections.intro: Escalate when findings suggest infection extending beyond uncomplicated middle-ear disease.

items.title: Mastoiditis
urgentFeatures: Post-auricular swelling, erythema or marked mastoid tenderness.
Persistent fever or systemic illness with worsening otalgia.
implications: Urgent same-day ENT or hospital assessment is required.

items.title: Intracranial or neurological complication
urgentFeatures: Severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia or repeated vomiting.
Altered consciousness, seizure or focal neurological deficit.

items.title: Severe systemic illness
urgentFeatures: Physiological instability, marked lethargy or clinical concern for sepsis.
Unable to maintain hydration or oral treatment.
implications: Use the appropriate acute illness or paediatric emergency pathway.

sections.title: Focused examination
sections.intro: Examine both ears and the surrounding structures. Otoscopy should be interpreted alongside symptoms and the overall clinical condition.

items.title: General assessment
howToTest: Assess overall appearance, hydration and systemic illness.
Assess pain and ability to drink.
normal: Clinically stable, hydrated and able to take oral treatment.
abnormal: Marked systemic illness, dehydration or physiological instability.
implications: Systemic condition may determine disposition even when local ear findings appear uncomplicated.

items.title: Otoscopy
howToTest: Inspect the external canal and tympanic membrane with adequate illumination.
Assess membrane colour, position, translucency and integrity.
Look for bulging, loss of landmarks, middle-ear effusion, perforation or discharge.
normal: Normal translucent tympanic membrane without bulging or middle-ear effusion.
abnormal: Bulging or inflamed tympanic membrane, loss of normal landmarks, middle-ear effusion, perforation or otorrhoea.
implications: Compatible otoscopic abnormalities support acute otitis media; canal-predominant inflammation suggests otitis externa.

items.title: Mastoid and surrounding ear
howToTest: Inspect and palpate the mastoid and post-auricular area.
Assess pinna position and surrounding swelling.
normal: No post-auricular swelling, erythema or marked mastoid tenderness.
abnormal: Post-auricular swelling, erythema, marked tenderness or displaced pinna.
implications: Consider mastoiditis and urgent ENT assessment.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
sections.intro: Consider alternatives when otoscopy or symptom pattern is not typical for middle-ear infection.

items.title: Important alternatives
commonFindings: Otitis media with effusion without acute infection.
Viral upper-respiratory infection with referred ear discomfort.
Pharyngitis or tonsillitis with referred otalgia.

sections.title: Management and disposition
sections.intro: Most uncomplicated acute otitis media improves without immediate antibiotics. Base treatment on age, severity, complication risk and ability to access reassessment.

items.title: Uncomplicated acute otitis media
mustConfirmOrExclude: Provide appropriate analgesia and hydration advice.
Use the current antimicrobial prescribing pathway where antibiotics are indicated.
Give clear advice about expected improvement and when reassessment is required.

items.title: Community management is appropriate when
mustConfirmOrExclude: No mastoid, neurological or systemic red flags are present.
Pain and hydration can be managed.
The patient or carer understands the plan and can access reassessment.

items.title: Escalate or refer
urgentFeatures: Any mastoid, intracranial, facial nerve or severe systemic feature.
Rapid deterioration or inability to maintain oral treatment.
implications: Use the appropriate ENT, paediatric or emergency pathway.

sections.title: Safety-netting
sections.intro: Give clear deterioration advice and expected recovery guidance.

items.title: Advise reassessment if
safetyNetting: Post-auricular swelling, redness or increasing mastoid pain develops.
Severe headache, neck stiffness, vomiting, altered behaviour or facial weakness develops.
Hydration deteriorates or the patient becomes systemically very unwell.
Symptoms are not improving as expected.
